title: Hats on a flat torus: how much must be left uncovered?
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: The hat tile can cover the plane, but never in a repeating pattern, so copies of the hat can never exactly cover a flat torus (a doughnut-shaped surface that is flat, like a video-game screen that wraps around). Packing hats on a torus of area A always leaves some area uncovered. Show that the least uncovered area grows without bound as A grows, and find how fast it grows. Cutting a square out of a hat tiling shows it is at most a constant times the square root of A.
math: Let $H$ be the hat polykite (area normalised to $1$); copies may be rotated and reflected. For a lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^2$ of covolume $A$, a packing of $T_\Lambda=\mathbb R^2/\Lambda$ is a finite family of isometric copies of $H$ in $T_\Lambda$ with disjoint interiors (each copy embedded). Let $g(A)=\inf_{\Lambda:\,\mathrm{covol}(\Lambda)=A}\ \inf_{\text{packings}}\ \big(A-\#\text{copies}\big)$. Trivially $g(A)=O(\sqrt A)$. (i) Prove $g(A)\to\infty$ as $A\to\infty$. (ii) Determine the order of growth of $g$; in particular, is $g(A)\asymp\sqrt A$? Board target (the Lean Claim): (i); the infimum ranges over all lattices of covolume $A$, including arbitrarily thin tori. (ii) is a further question.
